To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the timekeeping and time synchronization environments of a satellite in a low earth orbit (LEO) are more challenging than those of a satellite in geostationary orbit (GSO), and that the timekeeping environment of a satellite in an elliptical orbit (e.g., a Molniya orbit) is more challenging than that of a satellite in LEO.

the timekeeping and time transfer environment of a space-based clock ensemble is a function of the orbital parameters of each satellite, the timekeeping algorithm, the timekeeping hardware, and the time transfer protocol.
the accuracy and precision of timekeeping and the performance of time dissemination are dependent on the orbital and flight environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a timekeeping and time synchronization architecture for a distributed space-based clock ensemble.
developing the theory, algorithms, and hardware for the next generation of space-based clocks and time dissemination systems.
the development of algorithms and software for a distributed clock ensemble.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the timekeeping and time transfer environment for space-based systems is very challenging and must be addressed in the development of the next generation of positioning and navigation systems.
the clock ensemble is the most accurate timekeeping system in existence.
the next generation architecture should be based on a distributed clock ensemble.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the timekeeping environment for the next generation architecture is more challenging than the current GPS environment.
the next generation of space-based timekeeping and time transfer will be based on a network of clocks that are distributed throughout a constellation of satellites.
a distributed clock ensemble is a viable option for a future GNSS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a distributed space clock ensemble will have a significant impact on the next-generation space and terrestrial positioning systems.

the next generation GNSS architecture must consider the timekeeping environment of the space segment in order to provide the most accurate and reliable timekeeping and time synchronization for the terrestrial users.
the next generation of GNSS will require a new architecture to support a distributed space-based clock ensemble.
